acceptanceCriteria: A decision records whether missing pinned objects get their own code on both stable consumers, with a shared vector if yes, and CEM-V1-103 cites the chosen code.
body: Observed 2026-10-12 during V1-1275 (CEM-V1-103 evidence, internal/cem/convert TestCEMV1103ConvertUnavailableObjects): verifying a converted map whose bind commit is absent from the repository gives UNSUPPORTED repository git-read-failed on internal/cem/verify/stable.go, interop/cem01-go and the 0.2 verifier. Decision 0525 section 4 asks for an explicit unavailable outcome; git-read-failed also covers plain I/O faults, so a reader cannot tell a missing object from a broken repository. Question: should a distinct repository-object-unavailable code (or an axis value) be owned by the stable spec, and which stage reports it?
title: Unavailable pinned Git objects surface as git-read-failed, not repository-object-unavailable, on the stable consumers
